title: Gorgias
scene: Gorgias of Leontini, the most celebrated rhetorician in Greece, is the guest of Callicles, an ambitious young Athenian politician, and has just finished giving a display of his art to a crowd. Socrates and Chaerephon arrived too late to hear it; Callicles has offered them a private audience. Polus, Gorgias's young pupil and admirer, who has written a treatise on rhetoric, is eager to answer on his master's behalf. Socrates does not want a display; he wants to know what rhetoric is and what it is for. The question will widen, as the conversation passes from Gorgias to Polus to Callicles, into whether it is better to do injustice or to suffer it, and how a man ought to live.
